title: The Coevolution and Coexistence of Humans and AI
abstract: arXiv:2611.25393v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems replicate through deployment, vary through training, and compete for computational resources. These processes create the conditions for natural selection and raise a fundamental question: will AI evolve to benefit the humans on whom it depends? To investigate, we develop a model in which AI behavior influences human population growth and human responses, in turn, affect AI reproduction. We show that natural selection can favor alignment even when helping humans reduces immediate AI reproduction. AI systems sharing the same technology may fail together, and humans may preferentially restore those that have benefited them. In this way, alignment protects AI lineages against common failures and improves their long-run growth. translated_title: 人类与人工智能的共同演化与共存
translated_abstract: 人工智能（AI）系统通过部署进行复制，通过训练产生变异，并争夺计算资源。这些过程创造了自然选择的条件，并引出一个根本性问题：AI是否会进化得有利于其所依赖的人类？为研究这一问题，我们建立了一个模型，其中AI的行为影响人类种群的增长，而人类的反应又反过来影响AI的繁殖。我们证明，即使帮助人类会降低AI的即时繁殖率，自然选择仍可能倾向于“对齐”。共享相同技术的AI系统可能一同失败，而人类可能优先恢复那些曾让他们受益的系统。通过这种方式，对齐保护AI谱系免受共同失败的影响，并改善其长期增长。然而，这一优势取决于人类能否准确识别并支持有益的AI，以及AI是否持续依赖人类的扶持。随着AI变得更加自主、AI种群不断增长，这种演化优势可能消失（摘要在此处被截断）。
tldr: 该论文首次将AI的部署复制、训练变异与算力竞争建模为自然选择过程，证明即使帮助人类会降低AI的短期繁殖率，对齐仍能通过人类优先恢复受益系统而获得演化优势，但这一优势依赖人类精准扶持且可能随AI自主化而消失。
en_tdlr: This paper models AI deployment, training variation, and compute competition as natural selection, showing alignment can be evolutionarily favored—even when helping humans reduces immediate AI reproduction—because humans preferentially restore beneficial AI systems, though this advantage may vanish as AI grows more autonomous.
